Adesh Veerkumar Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra on 22
March, 2023
Bench: Surya Kant, J.K. Maheshwari

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Extraordinary Jurisdiction
 Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.6190/2021)
 Adesh Veerkumar Shah & Anr. Petitioner(s)
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra & Anr. Respondent(s)
 With
 Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl) No. 6247/2021
 O R D E R

1. The petitioners (Adesh Veerkumar Shah & Sangita Adesh Shah) in Special Leave Petition (Crl.)
No.6190 of 2021 and petitioner (Sham Tukaram Sawant) in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.6247 of 2021, seek grant of anticipatory bail in the case Crime No. 598 of 2019 registered with Andheri Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).

The FIR has been lodged on the complaint made by complainant (Maninderpal Singh Anand son of Trilochan Singh Anand).
2.
As per the allegations, there were two commercial projects, i.e., Project `A and Project `B which were to be developed by the petitioners.
On account of delay, a dispute arose between the developer and the complainant.
There was civil litigation also pending between the parties/their firms, before the criminal case was registered.

3. It may be mentioned that while issuing notice in both the Special Leave Petitions, interim protection against arrest was granted to the petitioners, subject to deposit of a sum of Rs.3/
 Crore with the Registrar (Judicial) of this Court within four weeks.

Thereafter, further statement was made on behalf of the petitioners on 16 09 2022 that they are willing to deposit a sum of Rs.2/
Crores in addition to Rs.3/
 Crores which had already been deposited.

At that stage, learned counsel for the complainant pointed out that the petitioners had agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.7.11/
Crores.

Subsequently, learned counsel for the petitioners was directed to have instructions along Adesh Veerkumar Shah vs The State Of Maharashtra on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112904204/
1 with payment schedule for deposit of an additional amount of Rs.4.11/
 Crores.

sentences.text:
These observations/
directions were issued as the parties were inclined to settle the disputes amicably.

4. This Court thereafter noticed on 12 12 2022 that the petitioners (builders) have agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.7.11/
 Crores to the complainant/intervenor as per the time schedule to be suggested by the parties and subject to the condition that the allotment of apartment in favour of the complainant/intervenor will be cancelled.
Since the complainant/intervenor agreed to the said suggestion, the parties were directed to work out the modalities for settlement.

5. It followed an order dated 12 01 2023 which reads as follows:
 1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. It appears that the settlement could not materialise between the parties pursuant to Order dated 12.12.2022 on account of minor issues which can be conveniently resolved.
3. The petitioners  builder undertake to give post dated cheques of Rs.4.11 crores in favour of the respondent complainant/intervenor within one week.
The receipt of the post dated cheques will ensure that the balance amount of Rs.4.11 crores is actually paid/received by the respondent  complainant/intervenor.
The post dated cheques in favour of the respondent  complainant/intervenor will be encashed on or before 31.12.2023.

4. Subject to giving the post dated cheques of the due amount by the petitioners  builder to the respondent   complainant/intervenor along with an affidavit of undertaking before this Court that all the cheques will be duly honoured, the respondent   complainant/intervenor agrees to the cancellation of allotment letter of the apartment within two weeks.

Similarly, the respondent  complainant/intervenor shall withdraw the cases filed against the petitioners   builder without prejudice to his legal rights including encashment of all the cheques for the balance amount of Rs.4.11 crores on or before 31.12.2023.
Learned counsel for the petitioners as well as learned counsel for respondent no.2   complainant

jointly state that in terms of order dated 12 01 2023, the parties have entered into a settlement, in terms whereof, the petitioners have handed over the post dated cheques for Rs.4.11/
 Crores dated 28 12 2023.
The petitioners have given an undertaking that the post dated cheques issued in favour of the complainant will be duly honoured.
7. In view of these developments, we are satisfied that ad interim protection against arrest granted to the petitioners vide order dated 27 08 2021 deserves to be made absolute.

8. Ordered accordingly.
9.

This will, however, be subject to the following conditions:

2

sentences.text: The needful shall be done within three weeks.

10. At this stage, it may be mentioned that I.A. No.58497 of 2023 has been fled by M/s. Kotwala Realty Pvt. Ltd. through its Director (Dinesh Jain) claiming that the sale consideration of Rs.3/
Crores was paid jointly by the said intervenor along and the complainant (Maninderpal Singh Anand) and that the allotment letter dated 12 12 2012 was also issued jointly in the names of M/s.
Popular Knitking and the said intervenor.
It is claimed that the intervenor is also entitled to pay ment of his share out of the amount which the petitioners have agreed to refund/paid to the complainant.

11. Since the issue raised by the intervenor is a disputed question of fact and he was not a party before the High Court or in the proceedings before the Sessions Court, we are not inclined to entertain its claim at this stage.

It will suffice to observe that the settlement between the petitioners and the complainant (Maninderpal Singh Anand), shall cause no prejudice to the rights and interests of the intervenor and it will be at liberty to avail its remedies in accordance with law.
12. The Special Leave Petitions are disposed of in above terms.

J (SURYA KANT) J (J.K. MAHESHWARI)
NEW DELHI 22ND MARCH,2023.
